label: Manor house
notes: a stone hall for the steward: rents are collected in full, the yard can be held, and a lord in residence settles the villages (owner 2026-09-13: build_days is how long the work takes at one day a step; the *_per_tick columns are what a finished building adds to the crown's metrics each tick; church_bonus is church_opinion per tick; produce_good/units join the ECONOMY column) civil_cost is what the work takes in CIVIL GOODS — the one price the game charges: MANOR_BUILD spends it, manor_demolish_refund returns a share of it to the stores, and it is the buildings' term in a manor's value. cost_gold is UNUSED by the game and kept for the library: hurrying is priced at build_rush_gold_per_day per day, so a full rush costs build_days x that. LAND AND PREREQUISITES (owner 2026-09-14): `land` says where the ground takes the building — any, or tokens joined by | of which ONE must hold: coast (a sea neighbour), high / peak (height at or above manor_focus_high_height / manor_focus_peak_height), town (a town stands in the manor), focus:<code> (the manor works that chief good), or a biome id; `prereq` names buildings (joined by |) that must ALL stand on the manor before this one is begun; `tier` is 1 for a first building, 2 and 3 for the ones that need others. EVERY building yields something once standing: its goods (produce_good/units, a month) or its *_per_tick and bonus columns.

label: Chapel
notes: a chapel with its own priest: the pulpit speaks well of the house that built it, and its chandler makes candles

label: Palisade
notes: a ditch and timber wall around the yard: a raid has to work for it, and the villages sleep easier

label: Granary
notes: a stone granary: the harvest keeps, a bad year is survived, and salted stores go to market — only where the land feeds it

label: Mill
notes: a water or wind mill on grain land: the manor grinds its own grain, takes a toll on its neighbours', and sends flour to the royal granaries

label: Fishing quay
notes: a jetty and boats: only on the coast

label: Saltworks
notes: pans and a boiling house: on the coast or the dry salt flats

label: Sawmill
notes: a saw-pit and timber sheds: only where there is forest to cut

label: Stonecutter
notes: a masons' lodge and a crane: on high ground or at a quarry

label: Mine shaft
notes: a timbered adit and headframe: in the hills or where iron is already worked

label: Apiary
notes: a bee yard among flowers and orchards

label: Winepress
notes: a press house and cellar: only where vines grow

label: Tannery
notes: hides into leather: only where herds or trappers bring the hides

label: Loom house
notes: weavers at their looms: where the sheep are, or in a town

label: Market
notes: a weekly market by charter: tolls and stall rents, and cloth changes hands — it needs a manor house to hold the charter

label: Smithy
notes: a forge by the mine: iron into tools

label: Brewery
notes: malt from the mill into ale: the villages are merrier

label: Shipwright
notes: a slipway beside the quay: boats and small ships

label: Abbey
notes: monks and a scriptorium where the chapel stood: the church warms, and books are copied

label: Castle
notes: a stone keep behind the palisade, the lord's hall within: very hard to take, and the land is quiet

label: Harbour
notes: a stone quay where the market meets the boats: harbour dues and a larger catch

label: Armoury
notes: a store of arms beside the smithy: weapons for the levy, and a harder yard
